design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Domain resolution must be request-scoped and passed explicitly through controller/service calls. No shared mutable global state may be introduced, and concurrent equities and crypto requests must not leak identifiers across responses.
forbidden_alternatives: Duplicating diagnostics or config controllers for crypto-only paths.
Hard-coding crypto identifiers into production response DTOs instead of selecting existing domain-scoped metadata.
Adding POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE config APIs as part of parity.
Introducing app-api persistence writes, background jobs, or unrelated ingest/runtime changes.
hard_constraints: Do not add new diagnostics endpoints.
Do not add config mutation paths.
Keep the change compact and read-only.
Do not change platform-dsl, platform-runtime, ingest modules, historical store schemas, or dag-framework snapshots.
Preserve equities behavior for domain=equities and default callers.
Crypto responses must not leak equities identifiers, venues, graph IDs, config versions, or diagnostics metadata.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: app-api owns query parameter parsing, request-scoped domain resolution, controller/service delegation, config response shaping, and diagnostics response shaping under app-api/src/main/java/com/ull/app/api/. QA owns acceptance tests and fixtures under tests/, qa/fixtures/, app-api/src/test/, app-api/src/test/java/, and ui/tests/. repo-memory records roadmap and decision updates only.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: No new persistence, writes, config mutation paths, diagnostics mutation paths, storage schemas, background refresh jobs, or app-api writes to Redis, QuestDB, local files, or databases. app-api continues to read existing hot runtime/config/diagnostics views.
design_contract.public_api: Preserve existing /api/config/* and /api/diagnostics/* routes and add or standardize optional ?domain=equities|crypto handling on every existing read endpoint. Response schemas stay compatible while runtimeConfigVersion, graphId, live config, partition state, diagnostics payloads, and venue identifiers become domain-correct.

final.problem_statement: Implement read-only crypto-domain parity for existing /api/config/* and /api/diagnostics/* endpoints so ?domain=crypto returns crypto runtime metadata while ?domain=equities and omitted domain preserve current equities behavior.
risk_register: Existing controllers may not share a single domain-resolution helper, creating uneven endpoint behavior unless the design inventories every route first.
Incomplete endpoint inventory could leave one config or diagnostics route still returning equities metadata for crypto.
Crypto hot-view keys or payload fields may differ from equities naming, requiring fixture-backed assertions to avoid accidental fallback to equities identifiers.
Default domain behavior could regress existing UI/API callers if omitted-domain semantics are changed.
Diagnostics service filtering may currently mix domain-aware and legacy no-domain hot-view reads, risking partial crypto responses.
Playwright selector-switch coverage may pass against UI state while API requests still omit ?domain unless network assertions inspect requested URLs or rendered domain-specific data.
Regression commands may depend on local services; blockers must be documented rather than bypassed.

design_contract.persistence_protocol: No new persistence, writes, config mutation paths, diagnostics mutation paths, storage schemas, background refresh jobs, or app-api writes to Redis, QuestDB, local files, or databases. app-api continues to read existing hot runtime/config/diagnostics views.

consolidated.problem_statement: Implement read-only crypto-domain parity for existing /api/config/* and /api/diagnostics/* endpoints so ?domain=crypto returns crypto runtime metadata while ?domain=equities and omitted domain preserve current equities behavior.
risk_register: Existing controllers may not share a single domain-resolution helper, creating uneven endpoint behavior unless the design inventories every route first.
Incomplete endpoint inventory could leave one config or diagnostics route still returning equities metadata for crypto.
Crypto hot-view keys or payload fields may differ from equities naming, requiring fixture-backed assertions to avoid accidental fallback to equities identifiers.
Default domain behavior could regress existing UI/API callers if omitted-domain semantics are changed.
Diagnostics service filtering may currently mix domain-aware and legacy no-domain hot-view reads, risking partial crypto responses.
Playwright selector-switch coverage may pass against UI state while API requests still omit ?domain unless network assertions inspect requested URLs or rendered domain-specific data.
Regression commands may depend on local services; blockers must be documented rather than bypassed.
